basics.description: Scales an EXISTING Segue install's resources up or down — Container App CPU/memory sizes, Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server SKU/storage, and Azure Managed Redis tier. This targets the SAME resource group and resources as your original install, it does not create a new environment. Enter the exact same deployment name prefix, Postgres/Redis/secrets mode, storage redundancy, passwords, API signing key, and current version tag you already have running — this wizard changes ONLY the size/SKU fields on later steps. Getting Postgres mode, Redis mode, secrets mode, or storage redundancy wrong doesn't just misconfigure something: it breaks connectivity or makes existing secrets unreachable (or, for storage redundancy, fails the deployment outright). WAF, Seq are left at main.bicep's own defaults by this limited wizard — if your original install customized those, use the full Segue Deploy-to-Azure wizard instead, or the CLI script containerization/scripts/upgrade-resources.ps1|sh, so nothing gets silently reset.

location.label: Region
location.toolTip: Must match the region your original Segue install already runs in.

basics.name: namePrefix
basics.label: Existing deployment name prefix
basics.toolTip: MUST match the prefix your original install used (e.g. <prefix>-app, <prefix>-postgres) — this is what makes this an in-place resize of the existing resources instead of a brand-new deployment.

constraints.validationMessage: Lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only, starting with a letter.

options.text: Every field below MUST match your original install exactly. Postgres mode, Redis mode, and secrets mode determine which real resource (and which real secret store) the app connects to at runtime — getting any of these wrong doesn't fail the deployment, it deploys successfully and then the app can't find its database, cache, or secrets. Storage redundancy and the version tag are checked/applied at deploy time instead: storage redundancy cannot be changed after the storage account exists at all (picking the wrong one fails the deployment outright: PreflightValidationCheckFailed / StorageAccountTypeConversionNotAllowed), and leaving the version tag wrong would redeploy a different application version as a side effect of resizing.

elements.name: storageRedundancy
elements.label: Storage redundancy
elements.toolTip: MUST match what your original install actually has — check the storage account's Redundancy setting in the Portal (or the resourceManifest output from your original deploy) if unsure. This cannot be changed after the storage account exists; picking the wrong value fails this deployment.

elements.name: postgresMode
elements.label: Postgres deployment type
elements.toolTip: MUST match your original install. Managed = Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server. Containerized = a Postgres container in this same environment.

elements.name: postgresPassword
elements.toolTip: The SAME Postgres password your original install used.

constraints.validationMessage: At least 8 characters, including upper case, lower case, and a digit.

elements.name: jwtSigningKey
elements.toolTip: The SAME API signing key your original install used — changing this invalidates every existing login session and refresh token.

elements.name: redisMode
elements.label: Redis deployment type
elements.toolTip: MUST match your original install. Containerized = a Redis container in this same environment (self-signed TLS cert). Managed = Azure Managed Redis.

elements.name: redisPassword
elements.toolTip: The SAME Redis password your original install used.

elements.name: redisTrustedCertificateThumbprint
elements.label: Redis TLS certificate thumbprint
elements.toolTip: The SAME thumbprint your original install used (see generate-cert.ps1|sh).

elements.name: secretsMode
elements.label: Tenant/app secret storage
elements.toolTip: MUST match your original install. If your original install used Azure Key Vault, picking Local database here will make the app unable to find secrets that only exist in that vault (SecretNotConfiguredException at runtime) — and vice versa.

elements.name: imageTag
elements.label: Currently running version tag
elements.toolTip: Pick the version tag your install is CURRENTLY running, listed newest-first with the date each was pushed. This wizard does not change it, but it must be supplied so the resize doesn't accidentally roll the app back to an older/default image. NOTE: this dropdown is populated by publish-deploy-artifacts.ps1|sh at publish time (from `az acr repository show-tags`) - these placeholder tokens are only ever uploaded after that substitution runs.

elements.name: postgresSize
elements.label: Postgres size
elements.toolTip: Containerized Postgres container size. Only used when your install's Postgres deployment type is Containerized.

elements.name: redisSize
elements.label: Redis size
elements.toolTip: Only used when your install's Redis deployment type is Containerized.

elements.name: segueAppSize
elements.label: Segue app size
elements.toolTip: Runs both FHIRBridge.Api and FHIRBridge.Gateway in this one container.

elements.name: workerSize
elements.label: Worker size
elements.toolTip: Background scheduler/pipeline processor — no HTTP endpoint.

elements.name: azurePostgresqlSku
elements.label: Managed Postgres pricing tier
elements.toolTip: Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server compute/pricing tier. Only used when your install's Postgres deployment type is Managed.

elements.name: azurePostgresqlStorageMb
elements.label: Managed Postgres storage
elements.toolTip: Azure only allows scaling this UP, never down — picking a value smaller than your current storage will fail. Only used when your install's Postgres deployment type is Managed.

elements.name: azureCacheForRedisTier
elements.label: Azure Managed Redis SKU
elements.toolTip: Only used when your install's Redis deployment type is Managed.

options.text: This wizard changes only container/database/cache sizing — every field on the earlier step must match your original install exactly (Postgres/Redis/secrets mode, storage redundancy, passwords/keys, current version). WAF and Seq are left at main.bicep's own defaults (both off); if either was enabled on the original install, use the full Deploy-to-Azure wizard instead with the same custom values plus these new sizes, so it isn't silently disabled.
